chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Batal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
"The Day We shall call every people by their Imam."
He عليه السلام said: "Their Imam is the one who is present among them, and he is the Qa'im of the people of his time."

key_terms.أَهْلِ زَمَانِهِ: the people of his era or time
key_terms.إِمَامِهِمْ: their Imam, the divinely designated leader by whom they are identified
key_terms.بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِهِمْ: among them, present in their midst
key_terms.قَائِمُ: the one who stands as holder of authority over the affair

ai.seo_question: Who is meant by the Imam in the verse 'The Day We shall call every people by their Imam'?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase about calling people by their Imam as referring to the Imam present among them in their own time. It emphasizes recognition of the divinely appointed Imam of each age and presents the verse as evidence for ongoing religious authority.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim Al Batal, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,
[17:71] The Day when We will Call every human being with their Imam
’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Their Imam<sup>asws</sup> would be that who will be in appearance before them, and he<sup>asws</sup> is Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> of the people of his<sup>asws</sup> era’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from ‘Abdallah ibn al-Qasim al-Batal from ‘Abdallah ibn Sinan who has said the following.
“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the meaning of , ‘On the day when We will call every nation with her Imam (leader) . .”
[17:71] The Imam (a.s.) said, “It refers to the Imam who is with them and he is al-Qa’im of the people of that time.”
